statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, let $f_1,\ldots,f_c$ be global functions on $X$, and let $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ be their common vanishing subscheme. For each $p\geq0$, define the local Gysin morphism
$$\gamma^p_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\longrightarrow\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$$
by the local cohomology/Čech class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$, for a lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$. Then the Gysin maps commute with the de Rham differentials:
$$d\circ\gamma^p_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}=\gamma^{p+1}_{f_1,\ldots,f_c}\circ d.$$
hypotheses: $Z$ is cut out by the given functions on $X/S$, and $\gamma^p$ is the indicated local-cohomology Gysin map.
conclusions: The Gysin morphisms form a chain map with respect to the de Rham differential.

statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.

These local constructions glue independently of the choice of defining functions to a canonical global morphism of sheaves on $Z$, for every $p\geq0$:
$$\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\longrightarrow\mathcal H_Z^c(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}).$$
hypotheses: $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a finitely presented closed immersion with locally free conormal sheaf of rank $c$.
conclusions: The locally specified Gysin maps for relative differential forms glue to a global canonical morphism into local cohomology supported on $Z$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-gysin-global}
Let $X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes. Let $Z \to X$ be a closed immersion
of finite presentation whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal{C}_{Z/X}$ is
locally free of rank $c$. Then there is a canonical map
$$
\gamma^p : \Omega^p_{Z/S} \to \mathcal{H}^c_Z(\Omega^{p + c}_{X/S})
$$
which is locally given by the maps $\gamma^p_{f_1, \ldots, f_c}$
of Remark \ref{remark-gysin-equations}.

statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.

For all $p\geq0$, the canonical global Gysin maps $\gamma^p$ commute with exterior differentiation: the square
$$\begin{array}{ccc}\Omega^p_{Z/S}&\xrightarrow{\gamma^p}&\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})\\
\downarrow d&&\downarrow d\\
\Omega^{p+1}_{Z/S}&\xrightarrow{\gamma^{p+1}}&\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c+1}_{X/S})\end{array}$$
commutes.
hypotheses: $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a finitely presented closed immersion with locally free conormal of rank $c$, and $\gamma^p$ is its canonical Gysin map.
conclusions: The global Gysin maps commute with the de Rham differential.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-gysin-differential-global}
Let $X \to S$ and $i : Z \to X$ be as in Lemma \ref{lemma-gysin-global}.
The Gysin map $\gamma^p$ is compatible with the de Rham
differentials on $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^\bullet_{Z/S}$.

statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.
Assume further that $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Koszul regular. Then $\mathcal H^j_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})=0$ for $j<c$, and the local-cohomology Gysin morphism induces maps
$$\gamma^{p,q}:H^q(Z,\Omega^p_{Z/S})\longrightarrow H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}).$$
These are compatible with the maps induced by the de Rham differential: for each $p,q$, $d\circ\gamma^{p,q}=\gamma^{p+1,q}\circ d$ (the target in the first composite has differential form degree $p+c+1$).
hypotheses: $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is a Koszul-regular finitely presented closed immersion of codimension $c$.
conclusions: The Hodge-level Gysin maps induced by local cohomology commute with exterior differentiation.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-gysin-differential-hodge}
Let $X \to S$ and $i : Z \to X$ be as in Lemma \ref{lemma-gysin-global}.
Assume $X \to S$ is smooth and $Z \to X$ Koszul regular.
The Gysin maps $\gamma^{p, q}$ are compatible with the de Rham
differentials on $\Omega^\bullet_{X/S}$ and $\Omega^\bullet_{Z/S}$.

statement:
Let $X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes and $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ a finitely presented closed immersion whose conormal sheaf $\mathcal C_{Z/X}=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$ is locally free of constant rank $c\geq0$. Write $\mathcal H^c_Z(-)$ for the $c$th local cohomology sheaf supported on $Z$. Locally where $Z$ is defined by $c$ functions $f_1,\ldots,f_c$, the Gysin morphism $\gamma^p:\Omega^p_{Z/S}\to\mathcal H^c_Z(\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ is given by a Čech/local-cohomology class represented by $\widetilde\omega\wedge df_1\wedge\cdots\wedge df_c/(f_1\cdots f_c)$ for a local lift $\widetilde\omega$ of $\omega$.
Assume $X\to S$ is smooth and $Z\hookrightarrow X$ is Koszul regular. Let $\gamma^{p,q}:H^q(Z,\Omega^p_{Z/S})\to H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S})$ be the Gysin map constructed from $\gamma^p$ and the map from cohomology with support to ordinary cohomology. Then for $\alpha\in H^q(X,\Omega^p_{X/S})$,
$$\gamma^{p,q}(i^*\alpha)=\alpha\cup\gamma^{0,0}(1)\quad\text{in }H^{q+c}(X,\Omega^{p+c}_{X/S}),$$
where $1\in H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)$.
hypotheses: $Z$ is Koszul regular of codimension $c$, $X/S$ is smooth, and $\alpha\in H^q(X,\Omega^p_{X/S})$.
conclusions: The Gysin pushforward satisfies the projection formula for the restriction $i^*\alpha$.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-gysin-projection-global}
Let $X \to S$, $i : Z \to X$, and $c \geq 0$ be as in
Lemma \ref{lemma-gysin-global}. Assume $X \to S$ smooth and
$Z \to X$ Koszul regular. Given $\alpha \in H^q(X, \Omega^p_{X/S})$ we have
$\gamma^{p, q}(\alpha|_Z) = \alpha \cup \gamma^{0, 0}(1)$ in
$H^{q + c}(X, \Omega^{p + c}_{X/S})$ with $\gamma^{a, b}$ as in
Remark \ref{remark-how-to-use}.

This is a nonvanishing result, not merely a well-definedness assertion.
statement:
Let $k$ be a field and let $X$ be an irreducible, smooth, proper $k$-scheme of dimension $d$. Let $i:Z=\{x\}\hookrightarrow X$ be the reduced closed subscheme defined by a $k$-rational point. The immersion has codimension $d$, so the Hodge Gysin map
$$\gamma^{0,0}:H^0(Z,\mathcal O_Z)=k\longrightarrow H^d(X,\Omega^d_{X/k})$$
is defined. Its value $\gamma^{0,0}(1)$ is nonzero.
hypotheses: $X$ is irreducible smooth proper of dimension $d$ over a field $k$, and $x\in X(k)$.
conclusions: The Hodge Gysin class of the rational point is nonzero in top Hodge cohomology.
original_source_statement_tex:
\label{lemma-class-of-a-point}
Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an irreducible smooth proper scheme over $k$
of dimension $d$. Let $Z \subset X$ be the reduced closed subscheme consisting
of a single $k$-rational point $x$. Then the image of
$1 \in k = H^0(Z, \mathcal{O}_Z) = H^0(Z, \Omega^0_{Z/k})$
by the map $H^0(Z, \Omega^0_{Z/k}) \to H^d(X, \Omega^d_{X/k})$
of Remark \ref{remark-how-to-use} is nonzero.
